info.bio:
Traffic fue un grupo de rock, procedente de Birmingham, Inglaterra. El grupo se formó en la década de los 60, y estuvo liderado por Steve Winwood, con Jim Capaldi, Chris Wood, y Dave Mason, Winwood se unió a la banda después de dejar de lado al grupo con el que tocaba hasta entonces, el Spencer Davis Group.

Los cuatro componentes del grupo colaboraron conjuntamente con un grupo llamado The Elbow Room, en Aston, Birmingham. Mason y Capaldi estaban ansiosos por formar un grupo

scenes.name: Rock progresivo
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Al emigrar a Gran Bretaña, el rock se convierte en mercancía de moda pero también se descontextualiza: lo que en EE UU era el diario de la juventud se vuelve en Gran Bretaña un ensayo. El progresivo no comenta la cultura juvenil sino que busca la innovación técnica: arranca con las óperas rock (S.F. Sorrow, Tommy) y los álbumes conceptuales, lo cimentan Traffic, Jeff Beck, Jethro Tull, Family y Genesis, y alcanza su cima con King Crimson (In The Court Of The Crimson King), Van Der Graaf Generator y Yes. Colosseum, la Third Ear Band (inventores de la world music), las variantes góticas (High Tide, Black Widow) y folk (Comus, Strawbs), Gentle Giant, Emerson Lake & Palmer y Roxy Music, que revoluciona el género y prepara la new wave y el synth-pop.

xref.title: Engine Failures and Emergency Communication (October 20, 1977)
xref.body: Around 6:40 PM, roughly halfway through the trip, the right engine, which had sounded problematic from the start, sputtered and died. At 6:42 PM, Captain McCurray contacted Houston Air Route Traffic Control, requesting the closest airport, and was directed to McCone Pike County Airport in McCone, Mississippi, about 17 kilometers behind them. Before the plane could turn, the left engine also failed, rendering hydraulics and steering inoperative. "Around halfway through the trip, at 6.40pm, the right engine, which didn't sound good to begin with, spotted and then died."

xref.title: Vehicular Manslaughter of Razzle (1984)
xref.body: In 1984, Vince Neil and Razzle, the drummer for Hanoi Rocks, left a party in Neil's powerful 1972 Ford Pantera to get more alcohol. While driving 65 mph in a 25 mph zone, Neil hit a wet patch, crossed into oncoming traffic, and crashed into two cars. Razzle died in the hospital, and Neil suffered cuts and cracked ribs. "While going 65 in a 25 miles per hour zone, the Pantera hit a wet patch of pavement, it crossed over into the opposite lane and crashed into two cars traveling the other way."

xref.title: Investigation for Black Ice (September 27, 1986)
xref.body: Following Cliff Burton's fatal bus accident, James Hetfield searched the highway extensively for the reported black ice but couldn't find any. This contributed to rumors surrounding the cause of the accident, though an investigation later ruled it a routine winter traffic accident. "James Headfield went up and down the highway looking for this black ice but he couldn't find any."

xref.title: Missed Pan Am Flight 103 (1988)
xref.body: Johnny Lydon and his wife, Nora, narrowly missed Pan Am Flight 103 on December 21, 1988, which was later bombed over Lockerbie, Scotland. Delays caused by Nora taking too long to pack, a subsequent argument, and getting stuck in traffic on the way to Heathrow Airport meant they missed the flight by minutes, thus saving their lives. "Nora, his wife, took too long to pack. They had a big fight, which delayed them even more, and then they got stuck in traffic on the way to Heathrow. They missed their flight by minutes."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Near-Miss Lockerbie Bombing (1988)
xref.body: John Lydon, of the Sex Pistols and Public Image Limited, came very close to dying in the bombing of Pan Am Flight 103 over Lockerbie, Scotland, on December 21, 1988. He and his wife, Nora, had seats on the flight but missed it by minutes due to his wife taking too long to pack, which caused a big fight, and then getting stuck in traffic on the way to Heathrow Airport. "Johnny Leiden with public image limited and death disco. He came very, very close to dying in the Lockerbie bombing in December of 1988."

xref.title: Legal Troubles (1996)
xref.body: In August 1996, at the peak of his fame, Lawrence was arrested for carrying a loaded handgun in a suitcase at Hollywood Burbank Airport. Months earlier, he had been detained for wandering into traffic and screaming curses in Assurement Oaks, California. No charges were filed in either case, but his problematic behavior began to overshadow his talent. "In August 1996, at the peak of his popularity and fame, Lawrence was arrested for carrying a loaded handgun in a suitcase at Hollywood Burbank Airport."

xref.title: Internet Unprofitability of In Rainbows (2007)
xref.body: Despite the success of the "In Rainbows" pay-what-you-want model, it was later revealed that 60% of the traffic to inrainbows.com resulted in no profit for the band beyond the credit card processing fees, as users either paid only the minimum or downloaded the album from torrent sites after it was in the wild. "That means 60% of the traffic to in rainbows.com was unprofitable for everybody but the credit card companies."

xref.title: Extensive Session Work
xref.body: Jim Gordon was a highly prolific drummer, contributing to literally hundreds of songs for a wide array of prominent artists including George Harrison, Joe Cocker, Dave Mason, Gordon Lightfoot, Harry Nilsson, Frank Zappa, Art Garfunkel, Traffic, and Steely Dan. He even contributed to the first Muppet movie. "Gordon could be heard on literally hundreds of songs."

xref.title: Fatal Car-Jacking Attempt
xref.body: Rhett Forrester, the singer for the New York metal band Riot in the early 1980s, and later a member of groups like the Calgary-based The Black Symphony, was murdered on September 22, 1996. He was shot and killed during an attempted car-jacking while stopped at a traffic light in Tucker, Georgia, after refusing to give up his car. A confession to the crime emerged years later. "When he refused to give up his car, he was shot and killed. It took years before someone confessed to the crime."

xref.title: Road Incident with Mugger
xref.body: On the way to a gig in San Diego, while stuck in a traffic jam, Black Flag's van was cut off by a woman driving a large car. Mugger, a member of the entourage, was so frustrated that he hopped out of the van and dumped his yogurt through her car window. This led to the band being "busted," with Greg having to handle the conversation with the authorities to resolve the incident. "Mugger had had enough of her bolt-ish and hopped out of the van and dumped his yogurt through her window."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Tourist Landmark and Graffiti Tradition
xref.body: The studio's gate and crosswalk remain a global attraction, drawing fans who frequently stop traffic for photos and write graffiti on the wall alongside the sidewalk. The wall is periodically whitewashed, only for the graffiti to reappear. "That gate in front of the studio, and that crosswalk are still there, and people come from all over the world to stop traffic into right graffiti on the wall that runs along the sidewalk in front of the building."
